facts.function: RCA supplies right heart, SA/AV nodes, inferior LV (usually); LCA supplies most of LV and anterior septum
facts.attachments: Arise from right and left aortic sinuses just above aortic valve → run in coronary sulcus

facts.function: Supplies anterior LV wall, anterior two-thirds of IV septum and apex; most commonly occluded coronary artery (anterior MI)
facts.attachments: Branch of LCA → anterior interventricular sulcus toward apex; gives diagonal and septal perforator branches

facts.function: Supplies LA and lateral/posterior LV wall; gives obtuse marginal branches
facts.attachments: Branch of LCA → left in coronary sulcus around to posterior heart; gives PDA in left-dominant hearts

facts.function: Supplies lateral (obtuse margin) wall of left ventricle
facts.attachments: Branch of circumflex artery → descends along obtuse (left) margin of heart

facts.function: Supplies posterior one-third of IV septum, inferior LV wall and posteromedial papillary muscle
facts.attachments: Usually from RCA (right-dominant ~70–85%) → posterior interventricular sulcus; from circumflex in left-dominant hearts

facts.function: Supplies lateral wall of right ventricle
facts.attachments: Branch of RCA → runs along acute (right inferior) margin of heart toward apex

facts.function: Collects most cardiac venous blood and returns it to the right atrium; dilates with pulmonary hypertension
facts.attachments: Posterior coronary sulcus → opens into RA between IVC opening and tricuspid orifice

facts.function: Drains anterior heart (LAD territory)
facts.attachments: Anterior interventricular sulcus with LAD → coronary sulcus with circumflex → becomes coronary sinus

facts.function: Drains posterior/inferior ventricles and posterior septum
facts.attachments: Posterior interventricular sulcus with PDA → coronary sinus near its right end

facts.function: Drains right margin of heart (posterolateral RA and RV)
facts.attachments: Accompanies right marginal artery → right coronary sulcus with RCA → coronary sinus

facts.function: Main systemic artery carrying LV output; ascending, arch and descending (thoracic) parts
Carries LV output; its only branches are the right and left coronary arteries (from aortic sinuses)
facts.attachments: Arises from LV at aortic valve → ascends within pericardium → aortic arch at sternal angle

facts.function: Distributes blood to head, neck and upper limbs via brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries
facts.attachments: Continues ascending aorta at sternal angle (T4) → arches posteriorly over left main bronchus → descending aorta at T4

facts.function: Supplies posterior intercostal, bronchial, esophageal, pericardial and superior phrenic arteries
facts.attachments: Continues arch at T4 in posterior mediastinum → aortic hiatus of diaphragm (T12) → abdominal aorta

facts.function: Supplies right side of head and neck and right upper limb
facts.attachments: First branch of aortic arch → ascends behind right sternoclavicular joint → right common carotid and right subclavian

facts.function: Supplies left side of head and neck
facts.attachments: Second branch of aortic arch → ascends in left carotid sheath → bifurcates at C4 into internal and external carotids

facts.function: Supplies left upper limb; gives vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical and costocervical branches; proximal stenosis causes subclavian steal
facts.attachments: Third branch of aortic arch → between anterior and middle scalenes → axillary artery at lateral border of rib 1

facts.function: Carries deoxygenated blood from RV to the lungs
facts.attachments: Arises from RV conus arteriosus at pulmonary valve → bifurcates under aortic arch into right and left pulmonary arteries

facts.function: Carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs
facts.attachments: Branches of pulmonary trunk; right passes behind ascending aorta and SVC; left joined to arch by ligamentum arteriosum

facts.function: Remnant of fetal ductus arteriosus (shunted pulmonary trunk blood to aorta); left RLN hooks around arch beside it
facts.attachments: Connects origin of left pulmonary artery to inferior surface of aortic arch

facts.function: Formed by LV; site of apical impulse (PMI) and mitral valve auscultation
facts.attachments: Points anteroinferiorly to the left, at left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line

facts.function: Posterior surface formed mainly by LA (with some RA); receives the pulmonary veins
facts.attachments: Faces posteriorly toward T6–T9 vertebrae; separated from esophagus by pericardium (oblique sinus)

facts.function: Groove encircling heart between atria and ventricles; contains RCA, circumflex artery, coronary sinus, small and great cardiac veins
Mark the interventricular septum: anterior holds LAD and great cardiac vein; posterior holds PDA and middle cardiac vein
Receiving chambers: RA gets systemic venous return (SVC, IVC, coronary sinus); LA gets oxygenated pulmonary venous return
Pumping chambers: RV to pulmonary trunk (anterior, thin-walled); LV to aorta (thickest wall, forms apex)
facts.supply: RV: RCA; LV: LAD and circumflex, inferior wall via PDA

facts.function: Separates ventricles; thick muscular part plus thin membranous part (most common VSD site); carries bundle of His branches
facts.supply: Anterior two-thirds: LAD septal perforators; posterior one-third: PDA

facts.function: Ear-like appendage of RA overlapping root of aorta; lined by pectinate muscles (primitive atrium derivative)
Right AV valve (anterior, posterior, septal leaflets); prevents RV → RA backflow in systole; heard at left lower sternal border
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterior, posterior and septal papillary muscles

facts.function: Remnant of fetal foramen ovale in interatrial septum; patent foramen ovale permits paradoxical emboli
facts.attachments: Floor from septum primum; rim (limbus fossae ovalis) from septum secundum

facts.function: Opening of SVC into upper smooth RA (sinus venarum); no valve; SA node lies at junction with crista terminalis
IVC opens into lower RA; valve of IVC (Eustachian) directed fetal oxygenated IVC blood toward foramen ovale
Coronary sinus opens into RA between IVC opening and tricuspid orifice; guarded by Thebesian valve; landmark of Koch triangle (AV node)
Parallel muscular ridges in auricles and anterior RA wall anterior to crista terminalis; derived from primitive atrium
Ridge separating smooth sinus venarum from rough pectinate RA; SA node lies at its upper end near SVC
facts.attachments: Runs from SVC opening to IVC opening; external correlate is sulcus terminalis

facts.function: RV papillary muscles: tense tricuspid chordae in systole, preventing leaflet prolapse
Largest RV papillary muscle; chordae to anterior and posterior tricuspid leaflets; moderator band attaches at its base
RV papillary muscle with chordae to posterior and septal tricuspid leaflets
Small RV papillary muscle arising from septum; chordae to anterior and septal tricuspid leaflets
Tendinous cords that prevent tricuspid leaflets from everting into the RA during systole
facts.attachments: Anterior, posterior and septal papillary muscles → tricuspid leaflets

facts.function: Coarse muscular ridges of RV inflow wall; outflow tract (conus arteriosus/infundibulum) is smooth
Carries right bundle branch from septum to anterior papillary muscle, coordinating its contraction; prevents RV overdistension
facts.attachments: Interventricular septum → base of anterior papillary muscle of RV

facts.function: Semilunar valve preventing pulmonary trunk → RV backflow in diastole; closure = P2; heard at left 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps (right anterior, left anterior, posterior) at outflow of RV conus arteriosus

facts.function: Return oxygenated blood from lungs to left atrium; ostia are common atrial fibrillation trigger sites (ablation target)
facts.attachments: Usually four (superior and inferior from each lung) → enter posterior wall of left atrium

facts.function: Ear-like appendage of LA overlapping pulmonary trunk; main site of thrombus formation in atrial fibrillation
Left AV valve (anterior and posterior leaflets); prevents LV → LA backflow in systole; heard at apex
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles; anterior leaflet continuous with aortic valve

facts.function: LV papillary muscles: tense mitral chordae in systole, preventing leaflet prolapse
LV papillary muscle with chordae to both mitral leaflets; rarely ruptures
LV papillary muscle with chordae to both mitral leaflets; most prone to rupture after inferior MI (acute mitral regurgitation)
Tendinous cords that prevent mitral leaflets from prolapsing into the LA during systole
facts.attachments: Anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles → both mitral leaflets

facts.function: Fine muscular ridges of LV wall; outflow tract (aortic vestibule) is smooth
Semilunar valve preventing aorta → LV backflow in diastole; closure = A2; heard at right 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps; coronary arteries arise from aortic sinuses just above the right and left cusps
